title: IMAGEBIND: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
problem: Learning a true joint embedding across many modalities is infeasible with existing approaches because they require large quantities of multimodal data where all modalities and combinations co-occur with the same images.

Existing methods typically align only a single pair or a few visual modality pairs, so the final embeddings are limited to the modality pairs used for training and do not transfer directly across other modality pairs.
Unlocking zero-shot classification for non-image modalities usually requires explicit paired text supervision for each modality.
core_techniques: [3.2] IMAGEBIND uses pairs of modalities (I,M), where I represents images and M is another modality, to learn a single joint embedding. | 이미지를 공통 축으로 사용해 각 모달리티를 하나의 공동 임베딩 공간에 정렬하는 학습 절차
[3.2] we encode them into normalized embeddings: qi = f(Ii) and ki = g(Mi) where f,g are deep networks. | 이미지와 다른 모달리티를 각각 심층 인코더로 정규화된 임베딩으로 인코딩하는 구조
[3.2] are optimized using an InfoNCE [54] loss | 이미지-모달리티 쌍 정렬을 위해 InfoNCE 대조학습 손실을 사용하는 학습 기법
[3.2] we use a symmetric loss LI,M + LM,I. | 양방향 정렬을 위해 대칭 손실을 함께 사용하는 학습 방식

[3.2] IMAGEBIND uses modalities paired with images, i.e., pairs of the form (I,M) to align each the embeddings from each modality M to those from images. | 모든 모달리티를 이미지와의 쌍으로만 학습해 이미지 임베딩에 정렬하는 바인딩 전략

[3.2] We observe an emer- gent behavior in the embedding space that aligns two pairs of modalities (M1, M2) even though we only train using the pairs (I,M1) and (I,M2). | 이미지와 각각만 정렬했는데도 보지 않은 모달리티 쌍 사이 정렬이 발생하는 emergent alignment 메커니즘

limitations: [6] Our embeddings are trained without a specific downstream task, and thus lag the performance of specialist models.
[6] Our model is a research prototype and cannot be readily used for real world applications ( Appendix F).
[F] joint embedding may also create unintentional associations.
[F] IMAGEBIND leverages the image-text embeddings learned by a pretrained model on large web-based data which has biases as documented in different studies [60].
[F] These joint embeddings are thus limited to the concepts present in the datasets.
